🥘 Ingredients

  • 8 ounces dry penne pasta
  • 1 cup cherry tomatoes, halved
  • 1 medium zucchini, diced
  • 1 red bell pepper, diced
  • 2 tablespoons olive oil
  • 2 cloves garlic, minced
  • 1 teaspoon dried oregano
  • 1/2 teaspoon salt
  • 1/4 teaspoon black pepper
  • 1/4 cup fresh basil leaves, chopped
  • 1/4 cup grated Parmesan cheese (optional)

👩‍🍳 Instructions

  1. Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Add the penne pasta and cook for 7 minutes, which is about 2 minutes less than the package instructions. This ensures the pasta is slightly undercooked, so it won’t become mushy during air frying. Stir occasionally to prevent sticking. Drain the pasta and rinse briefly with cold water to stop cooking. This step is crucial because the air fryer will finish the cooking and create a crispy texture, so starting with pasta that’s just shy of done gives the best results.
  2. In a large bowl, combine the cooked pasta, halved cherry tomatoes, diced zucchini, and red bell pepper. Add minced garlic, olive oil, dried oregano, salt, and black pepper. Toss everything gently to coat the pasta and veggies evenly. The oil helps crisp the pasta and veggies in the air fryer, while the garlic and oregano add a fragrant base flavor. Make sure the veggies are cut into similar sizes so they cook evenly.
  3. Preheat your air fryer to 375°F (190°C) for about 3 minutes. Preheating is important because it ensures the pasta and veggies start crisping immediately when placed inside, which helps develop that golden texture and prevents sogginess. Without preheating, the food might steam instead of crisping up nicely.
  4. Place the pasta and veggie mixture into the air fryer basket. Spread it out evenly in a single layer to allow hot air to circulate freely. Crowding the basket can cause uneven cooking and soggy spots. Cook for 15 minutes, shaking the basket gently halfway through to turn the pasta and veggies for even browning. Keep an eye on the pasta towards the end to avoid burning.
  5. Once the pasta is crispy and golden, transfer it to a serving bowl. Sprinkle the fresh chopped basil over the top and toss gently. The fresh basil adds brightness and a fresh herbaceous note that balances the crispy, savory flavors. Adding it at the end keeps the herbs vibrant and aromatic.
  6. Optionally, sprinkle grated Parmesan cheese over the top while the pasta is still hot. The cheese melts slightly, adding a creamy, salty finish that complements the crispy texture. If you’re vegan or dairy-free, you can skip this or use a plant-based cheese alternative. Be careful not to add cheese too early in the air fryer, or it might burn.
  7. Serve immediately while the pasta is still crispy and warm. This dish pairs well with a simple green salad or crusty bread for a complete meal. If you let it sit too long, the pasta will soften as it cools, losing some of that delightful crunch.
  8. If you want to add a little extra flavor, drizzle a small amount of balsamic glaze or lemon juice over the top just before serving. The acidity cuts through the richness and brightens the dish. This is totally optional but a nice touch if you have it on hand.
  9. Clean your air fryer basket promptly after cooking to prevent leftover oil and food bits from sticking. A quick wipe with a damp cloth or mild soap and water keeps your appliance ready for the next use. Proper maintenance helps your air fryer last longer and prevents off-flavors in future dishes.

  • Cooking spray

👩‍🍳 Instructions

  1. Start by cooking the elbow macaroni in salted boiling water until just al dente, about 7-8 minutes. It’s important not to overcook the pasta here since it will cook a little more in the air fryer. Al dente pasta holds its shape and texture better, preventing mushiness later. Drain the pasta well and set aside. Be sure to save a small cup of pasta water just in case you need to loosen the sauce later—it’s a handy trick to keep your cheese sauce silky smooth.
  2. In a medium saucepan, melt the butter over medium heat. Once melted, whisk in the flour to create a roux. Cook this mixture for about 1-2 minutes, whisking constantly to avoid lumps and to cook out the raw flour taste. This step is crucial because the roux is the base that thickens your cheese sauce and gives it that velvety texture. If you rush it or skip cooking the roux, your sauce might taste floury or be too thin.
  3. Slowly pour in the warmed milk while whisking constantly to prevent lumps. Keep whisking until the mixture thickens and coats the back of a spoon, about 5-7 minutes. This gentle heating allows the starches in the roux to swell and thicken the sauce properly. If you add cold milk or pour too fast, you risk lumps forming and an uneven sauce texture.
  4. Remove the saucepan from heat and stir in 1 1/2 cups of shredded cheddar cheese, garlic powder, onion powder, salt, and pepper. Stir until the cheese is fully melted and the sauce is smooth. Adding the cheese off the heat prevents it from becoming grainy or separating. Use sharp cheddar for that classic tangy flavor and creamy melt.
  5. Combine the cooked pasta with the cheese sauce in a large bowl, mixing gently to coat every piece. If the sauce feels too thick, add a splash of reserved pasta water to loosen it up. This step ensures every bite is cheesy and creamy. Avoid overmixing to keep the pasta from breaking.
  6. Transfer the macaroni and cheese mixture into an air fryer-safe baking dish or pan. Sprinkle the remaining 1/2 cup of shredded cheddar cheese evenly over the top. This layer will melt and brown during air frying, creating that irresistible cheesy crust.
  7. Mix the panko breadcrumbs with a little melted butter to help them brown nicely. Sprinkle this mixture evenly over the cheese layer. The butter-coated breadcrumbs crisp up beautifully in the air fryer, giving you that coveted crunchy topping. Don’t skip the butter here—it’s what helps achieve the golden crust.
  8. Preheat your air fryer to 375°F (190°C). Place the baking dish inside and cook for 10-12 minutes until the cheese is bubbly and the top is golden brown. Keep an eye on it towards the end to avoid burning. This air fryer step is key to crisping the top without drying out the pasta underneath.
  9. For an extra crispy finish, switch your air fryer to broil mode and broil for 2-3 minutes. Watch carefully so it doesn’t burn. This last step adds an irresistible crunch and deep golden color to the topping, elevating your macaroni and cheese to restaurant-quality comfort food.

  1. Start by preheating your oven to 350°F (175°C) and lining a baking sheet with parchment paper. This ensures your cookies won’t stick and will bake evenly. Preheating is key so the cookies start cooking immediately, which helps them keep their shape and texture. Avoid skipping this step as it can cause uneven baking.
  2. In a large bowl, cream together the softened butter, granulated sugar, and brown sugar using a hand mixer or stand mixer on medium speed. Creaming incorporates air, making your cookies light and tender. Beat until the mixture is pale and fluffy, about 3-4 minutes. If you rush this step, the dough can be dense and the cookies won’t have that soft texture.
  3. Add eggs one at a time, mixing well after each addition, then stir in the vanilla extract. The eggs add moisture and structure, while vanilla brings a warm, sweet aroma that enhances the berries. Make sure to mix thoroughly so the eggs fully incorporate, which helps the dough bind properly.
  4. In a separate bowl, whisk together the all-purpose flour, baking soda, and salt. This step ensures the baking soda is evenly distributed, which helps the cookies rise uniformly. Skipping this can cause uneven texture or salty pockets in your cookies.
  5. Gradually add the dry ingredients to the wet mixture, mixing on low speed just until combined. Overmixing can develop gluten, leading to tougher cookies, so stop as soon as you see no more flour. The dough should be thick but soft.
  6. Gently fold in the fresh blueberries with a spatula, taking care not to crush them. This preserves their shape and prevents the dough from turning blue or too wet. Folding rather than mixing vigorously keeps the dough light and the berries intact.
  7. Scoop rounded tablespoons of dough onto the prepared baking sheet, spacing them about 2 inches apart to allow spreading. Using a cookie scoop helps keep sizes even, which ensures consistent baking. If cookies are too close, they’ll merge and lose their shape.
  8. Bake in the preheated oven for 12-15 minutes until the edges are golden and the centers look set but still soft. The baking time may vary slightly depending on your oven, so start checking at 12 minutes. Overbaking will dry out the cookies, so watch carefully.
  9. Remove the cookies from the oven and let them cool on the baking sheet for 5 minutes before transferring to a wire rack. This resting time lets them firm up without breaking. Moving them too soon can cause them to fall apart, while waiting too long can make them stick.

  1. Start by peeling your peaches. The easiest way is to score a small X at the bottom of each peach and blanch them in boiling water for about 30 seconds, then plunge them into ice water. The skins should slip right off. Peeling is important because the skin can be tough and bitter, which would throw off the fresh, sweet vibe of the salsa.
  2. Dice the peeled peaches into small, even pieces—about 1/2 inch. Uniform pieces help the salsa have a nice texture and make it easier to scoop. Avoid making the pieces too small or mushy, or the salsa will lose its fresh bite and look more like a puree.
  3. Next, finely chop the jalapeño, but be sure to remove the seeds and membranes if you want to keep the heat mild. If you like it spicy, leave some seeds in. Use a sharp knife and wash your hands afterward to avoid irritation. The jalapeño adds a subtle heat that balances the sweetness of the peaches perfectly.
  4. Chop the red onion finely as well. The onion adds a nice crunch and sharpness to the salsa. Be careful not to overpower the peaches, so keep the onion amount moderate. Rinse the chopped onion briefly under cold water if you want to mellow the bite.
  5. Roughly chop fresh cilantro leaves and stems. Cilantro brings a bright herbal note that complements the fruitiness and spice. If you’re not a fan, you can reduce the amount or substitute with fresh parsley, but cilantro really lifts the salsa.
  6. Combine the diced peaches, jalapeño, onion, and cilantro in a mixing bowl. Add the lime juice, salt, and black pepper. The lime juice not only adds brightness but also helps preserve the color of the peaches and melds all the flavors together.
  7. Gently toss everything together, making sure not to mash the peaches. You want to keep the salsa chunky and fresh. Taste and adjust seasoning as needed—sometimes a pinch more salt or lime juice makes all the difference.
  8. Let the salsa rest in the fridge for at least 30 minutes before serving. This resting time lets the flavors meld beautifully and the salsa chill nicely. It’s a key step that transforms it from good to great.
  9. Serve chilled as a topping for grilled chicken, fish, tacos, or simply with tortilla chips. The sweet and spicy combo is a crowd-pleaser that adds a fresh pop to any meal.
